Check and prepare distance data for fitting

Source: R/prepare.R
prepare_distance_data.Rd

Checks a table of detections and returns it in the form mrds::ddf() expects. sweep_models() calls it before fitting. It is exported so the checks can be run on their own before a sweep.

Usage

prepare_distance_data(data, truncation, left = NULL, breaks = NULL)

Arguments

data

Data frame, one row per detection. Needs a numeric distance column (exact) or numeric distbegin and distend columns (binned). Optional columns: object (detection ID) and distance_source.

truncation

Number. Right truncation distance, in the units of the distances. Required.

left

Number or NULL (default). Left truncation distance. NULL means no left truncation.

breaks

Numeric vector or NULL (default). Bin cutpoints for binned data, strictly increasing. Derived from the bins when NULL. Ignored, with a warning, for exact data.

Value

A list:

data

The prepared data frame, ready for mrds::ddf().

binned

TRUE for binned data, FALSE for exact.

breaks

The cutpoints used (binned), or NULL (exact).

n_dropped

Number of input rows not in data.

dropped

Named integer vector splitting the drops by reason: no_distance, beyond_truncation, inside_left. It shows whether truncation trimmed a tail or removed most of the survey.

Details

Distances are either exact (one distance per detection) or binned (an interval distbegin to distend per detection, as recorded by strip or band surveys). The two are fitted with different likelihoods.

How it works

The steps run in this order. The first refusal stops the function with an error.

  1. Check the arguments. data must be a data frame. truncation must be one positive finite number. left, if given, must be one non-negative finite number smaller than truncation.

  2. Check the distance columns. Any of distance, distbegin and distend that is present must be numeric (an all-NA column is allowed) and must not be negative.

  3. Decide the distance type. Refuse a table with no distances, and refuse a table with both exact and binned distances.

  4. Check distance_source, if present, on the rows with an exact distance. Refuse "break_off" distances. Warn about "circling" distances. Only rows that will be fitted (within left to truncation) are counted.

  5. Count, by reason, the rows that will be dropped: no distance, beyond truncation, or inside left.

  6. For binned data:

    1. Drop rows with a missing distbegin or distend.

    2. Refuse any distend of Inf.

    3. Drop bins that end beyond truncation or begin inside left.

    4. Refuse if no rows remain.

    5. Derive breaks from the bins, refusing bins that do not tile; or, if breaks is supplied, check that it contains every recorded bin edge.

    6. Refuse if the highest break is not truncation.

    7. Refuse if the lowest break is not left (or 0 when left is NULL).

    8. Remove the distance column.

  7. For exact data:

    1. Warn that breaks is ignored, if it was supplied.

    2. Remove the distbegin and distend columns.

    3. Drop rows with no distance, beyond truncation, or inside left.

    4. Refuse if no rows remain.

  8. Add an object column numbering the rows if there is none. Refuse duplicated object values.

Rows with no distance are how a flatfile records a sample with no detections, so dropping them is expected. Every dropped row is counted in the return value.

What it refuses and why

ConditionReason
Non-numeric distancesText or factor codes would be compared to truncation as text or level numbers, keeping the wrong rows.
Negative distancesA perpendicular distance has no side. Use abs() if the sign records the side of the line.
Exact and binned distances togetherThe two likelihoods differ, so their AICs cannot be compared in one sweep. Split the table on its distance-source column and sweep each part.
distance_source == "break_off"A break-off distance runs from where the aircraft left the line to the logged position. It is not perpendicular to the line.
distend of InfAn open top bin cannot be fitted. Drop those rows or close the bin. This applies even if truncation would drop the bin.
Bins that do not tile (derived breaks)If bins leave gaps or overlap, they do not define one set of cutpoints.
breaks missing a recorded bin edgeGoodness of fit is computed over breaks, so breaks must be the survey's own cutpoints.
Highest break not equal to truncationA binned fit integrates over the bins. A gap between the top bin and truncation is effort with no bin.
Lowest break not equal to left (or 0)The same gap at the near end. It occurs when the innermost bin had no detections, or when left falls inside a bin. Supply breaks to fix it.
No rows left after truncationThere is nothing to fit.
Duplicated objectmrds identifies detections by object.

What it warns about

  • distance_source == "circling": the animal's position while the aircraft circled, projected onto the line. It is a perpendicular distance, but measured minutes after the detection. distsamp::detection_data() excludes these rows unless include_circling = TRUE. They are kept, and the warning gives their count.

  • breaks supplied with exact distances: it is ignored.

See also

sweep_models()

Examples

d <- data.frame(object = 1:5, distance = c(10, 50, 120, NA, 900))
prep <- prepare_distance_data(d, truncation = 400)
prep$n_dropped
#> [1] 2
prep$dropped
#>       no_distance beyond_truncation       inside_left 
#>                 1                 1                 0 
prep$data
#>   object distance
#> 1      1       10
#> 2      2       50
#> 3      3      120
